article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Google Erases a Record $500 Billion as AI Eats Into Sales
post_text:
Alphabet's Q3 earnings miss last week erased more than $500 billion in market cap in a single session, its largest ever one-day plunge. Search ad revenue grew at its slowest pace in five quarters, while capital expenditures hit $51 billion in the quarter alone and the company reiterated plans to spend $195–205 billion for the full year. The same week, Anthropic filed its S-1 targeting a valuation of $1.5 to $2 trillion, having posted an $80.7 billion net loss in just the first half of 2026.

The Alphabet selloff is a pressure test on the entire AI investment thesis. When the company best positioned to monetize AI search can't meet expectations while spending at that scale, it forces a harder question: who actually captures the return on all this capital?

A piece we published earlier this year argued that the real overlooked value in today's market sits not in AI at 30x revenue multiples, but in unglamorous, cash-generative businesses that nobody is writing breathless headlines about. Alphabet's miss, and Anthropic's staggering loss figures buried inside a blockbuster IPO filing, make that argument harder to dismiss than it was six months ago. The full piece is on our website.
